title: House on Haunted Hill

evidence.note: The Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures, Jan-Dec 1959 (archive.org, searched directly) carries the ORIGINAL registration under the film's exact release title, with no 'a': 'HOUSE ON HAUNTED HILL. Allied Artists Pictures Corp. 75 min., sd., b&w, 35 mm. (c) Allied Artists Pictures Corp.; 29Dec58 (in notice: 1959); LP12531.' This matches registration LP0000012531 exactly (same claimant, same date, same notice year) cited in the 1986 renewal below.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures, Jan-Dec 1959 (archive.org)

evidence.note: Renewal registration RE0000318809 (filed 1986-01-12) exists at the U.S. Copyright Office for a motion picture titled 'House on a haunted hill. By Allied Artists Pictures Corporation.', renewing original registration LP0000012531 (filed 1958-12-29, notice year 1959). The renewing party is listed as Revival Pictures (PWH). The 'a' in the renewal filing's title is a clerical variant, not a different work: the original 1959 registration (above) uses the exact release title with no 'a', and the claimant, filing date and notice year are identical. The renewal also lands in the correct 28th-year window (1959+27=1986). The film is therefore still under US copyright, protected until 1 January 2055 (95 years from the 1959 notice year).
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System

evidence.note: A registration and a 1986 renewal (reported as EU0000546955 and RE0000309723) are said to exist for a song 'House on Haunted Hill' (music by Richard Loring, lyrics by Richard Kayne). The cited Copyright Office page returned no record data when fetched, so this is unverified. A 1958 unpublished-composition registration renewed in 1986 is an unusual combination and needs a retrievable record. Until one is found, check the song's status separately before reusing it.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System (page returned no data)

evidence.note: No separate registration for a background score was located. The recorded soundtrack of a sound film normally shares the film's own status, which is undetermined here.
No underlying novel or play was identified, so no separate source work with its own term was found. The story follows the film's own copyright status, which is undetermined (see print layer).
USPTO trademark records were not searched. No active mark for the title could be confirmed or excluded. The title was reused for later remakes and sequels, so check before using it on new products.

A faithful restoration of a public-domain film adds no new US copyright: copying or restoring public-domain images without original creative additions is not protected (Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp., S.D.N.Y. 1999, following Feist v. Rural, 1991). Anything a restoration ADDS can be protected: a new score, colorization, newly written or translated titles, and other original additions. Separately, ripping a copy-protected Blu-ray or DVD can break the DMCA's anti-circumvention rule (17 U.S.C. 1201) even when the film itself is public domain.
evidence.source: Bridgeman Art Library v. Corel Corp. (summary)

evidence.note: 17 U.S.C. 1201 - circumvention of copyright protection systems.
Modern HD restorations and colorized versions can carry new protectable elements.

editorial:
William Castle's film puts Vincent Price in a mansion as a wealthy host who offers five strangers $10,000 each if they survive the night. It is a compact black-and-white horror title with a famous lead and a simple premise, and many copies circulate on the Internet Archive with uploader 'public domain' labels.

The film's US status is undetermined. A 1986 renewal (RE0000318809) is reported, but the Copyright Office page could not be read, and other public sources say no renewal was filed and the film is public domain. The release and publication year is also ambiguous (December 1958 versus 1959), so any term end date (1 January 2054 or 2055) is conditional and uncertain. Check the Copyright Office record or a CCE renewal volume before relying on either view. The theme song is a separate layer, with a reported but unverified 1986 renewal (RE0000309723).
faq: Can I upload or distribute the 1959 House on Haunted Hill?

Not safely until its status is checked. Internet Archive copies carry uploader labels, but those are claims, not rulings. A renewal is reported (RE0000318809) but could not be verified, and other sources say the film is public domain. Check the Copyright Office record first.
Is the theme song in the film public domain?

Undetermined. A 1986 renewal (RE0000309723) is reported for the composition (music by Richard Loring, lyrics by Richard Kayne), but it could not be verified. Get a retrievable record or clear the song before any new recording.
